overview: Two complementary components of a laboratory quality management system, one focused on checking test results and the other on the whole process.
genZNote: QC checks if today's run is any good. QA makes sure the whole system doesn't let bad runs happen in the first place.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The set of procedures used to monitor and verify the accuracy and reliability of test results, typically by running known control materials alongside patient samples.
aspects.valueB: The overall, systematic program of policies and procedures designed to ensure quality throughout the entire testing process, from pre-analytic to post-analytic.

aspects.label: Scope
aspects.valueA: Narrow — focused on the analytical testing phase itself.
aspects.valueB: Broad — encompasses pre-analytic, analytic, and post-analytic phases, plus documentation, training, and equipment maintenance.

aspects.label: Focus
aspects.valueA: Reactive — detects errors in real time by monitoring control results.
aspects.valueB: Proactive — prevents errors by designing robust processes, protocols, and staff competency programs.

aspects.label: Example Activity
aspects.valueA: Running normal and abnormal control samples with each batch of patient tests and tracking them on Levey-Jennings charts.
aspects.valueB: Establishing standard operating procedures, staff training and competency assessment, and proficiency testing programs.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Day-to-day monitoring of test accuracy via control samples.
aspects.valueB: System-wide processes ensuring overall quality across the entire testing pathway.
